title.narrative: Boosting Colombia’s start-up ecosystem: Rockstart Web & Mobile Accelerator programme in Bogotá, Colombia

description.narrative: Due to a growing number of high quality Latin American start-ups and their interest in the Rockstart Accelerator Programme in the Netherlands, Rockstart decided to expand to the region and set-up the first “Web & Mobile” Rockstart Accelerator program in Bogotá, Colombia, with the support of Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA). The aim of the project was to strengthen and boost the local Colombian tech start-up ecosystem, inspire and support Latin American Web & Tech Entrepreneurs to start their start-up, educate around building a company and help them apply for the Rockstart Accelerator Program. They helped build the Colombian ecosystem including sharing knowledge with potential investors on what start-ups are, how to invest in them, what an accelerator is and explain them about the risk-return, as investing in start-ups requires a different approach than traditional investments. Colombian start-ups were provided with coaching, advice and feedback from investors mentors and audiences of their peers during events such as Rockstart Answers.During a 100-day accelerator programme, Rockstart directly employed 7 people and supported an additional 70 direct jobs, the founders and employees of the 10 start-ups that were selected. Indirectly, the project supported 160 jobs, of which 130 were female. Most direct and indirect jobs supported involved youth under 30. An additional 182 local investors as well as 65 start-ups received training as part of the project.Furthermore, the start-ups were introduced to potential partners, buyers and investors which resulted in rapid growth of their businesses. The project led to further private investments for Rockstart in Colombia, which is now fully operational and self-sufficient and running its third accelerator programme. Supported direct and indirect jobs have shown to be sustainable and start-ups from the first accelerator are growing with 9% per year and successfully scaling up, leading to additional job creation and investments in Colombia and the entire Latin American region.
